This plan changes package sources and managed templates only after separate plan approval; it does not authorize a commit, installation, configuration change, or release.

Execution bootstrap: use the approved GRACE lifecycle and a compatible session policy, not the current vvoc native checkpoint loader, to execute this GraceChangePlan. The current single-session policy can implement directly and permits the final independent reviewers. Do not depend on the new generic runtime to bootstrap its own implementation, switch the active orchestration profile, convert this bundle into a shadow .vvoc package, disguise reviewers, or install templates mid-session. Execution mode is resolved by grace-execute after plan approval.

Scope and ownership: source independence changes the product's generic guidance, not this repository's explicit GRACE approvals. Preserve AGENTS.md, schemas/vvoc/v3.json, package.json, model-role assignments, presets, host permissions, all active user/global configuration, and existing archives. No release or installation is authorized. The technology context's existing bunx/rc GRACE commands conflict with the explicit AGENTS.md stable-CLI policy; that policy resolves the command choice without guessing. Reconcile those two stale command references alongside owned technology context during T-008, not during planning.

Architecture: add M-WORKFLOW-CONTRACT at src/lib/workflow-contract.ts for dependency-free common types, declared-file normalization, bounded contract validation, and exact-reference DAG validation. Add M-WORKFLOW-EXECUTION at src/plugins/workflow/execution.ts for the common execution registry, append-only amendments, explicit lineage, and completion prerequisites. Add M-WORKFLOW-AUTHORITY at src/plugins/workflow/authority.ts for provenance, advance authority, stage approvals, and reserve accounting. Keep review-generation reducers in checkpoints.ts and attempt/acceptance reducers in delegated.ts. checkpoint-io.ts remains the native adapter; neither generic execution nor authority parses arbitrary source documents. A transactions.ts helper belongs to M-PLUGIN-WORKFLOW and serializes state commits, not work scheduling.

Common contract: WorkflowExecution has runId, owning session, trusted workspaceRoot, stable executionKey, immutable source identity, contract revision, explicit execution boundary, task bindings, checkpoint obligations, lineage, authority/stage records, and preparing/active/sealed state. Source is a discriminated union of native-package, provided-plan, and conversation-scoped. Only native-package carries plan/spec paths, content hashes, and native definition metadata. Provided-plan stores a bounded opaque source reference, not parsed commands or a converted artifact; conversation-scoped needs no source file. Keep runId as the canonical runtime identifier and accept legacy planRunId/planTaskId bindings as checked aliases, not a second registry. Preserve existing native run IDs on upgrade.

Task and review contracts: a task has a stable taskId, title, bounded goal/acceptance/verification text, stable criterion identities, exact writeScope files, explicit task dependencies, optional blockedBy checkpoint IDs, and requiredReviewers. For a new delegated task, requiredReviewers may be [], [spec], [code], or [spec,code]; a nonempty set registers a deterministic single-task checkpoint and does not turn worker DONE into reviewer PASS or remove controller acceptance. Legacy implementation and review_only modes keep their existing reviewer-round semantics. Group checkpoints carry checkpointId, kind, covers, exact scope, requiredReviewers, acceptance criteria, verification references, and obligation origin (source, user, or controller). Native reviewer fields adapt to requiredReviewers without changing native XML. A checkpoint with an empty reviewer set is invalid; no assigned review is represented by no checkpoint.

Minimal generic entry: extend work_item_open with an optional top-level execution descriptor (executionKey, source, goal, scope boundary) or an existing runId, mutually exclusive, and bounded task-contract fields on items. One call may create an execution and its first task or a batch; a later call with runId appends tasks atomically. Existing unbound standalone work-item calls remain valid and do not gain invented source or authority on migration. For exact adoption into a generic run, accept existing workItemId bindings only when session, mode, key, scope, and stored contract agree; keep all counters/history. Work already bound to a native or another generic execution cannot be adopted to bypass its obligations.

Tool actions: preserve work_checkpoint register with planPath as the strict native input path, optionally binding a previously preparing native runId. Add register with runId and checkpoints for generic obligations; these forms are mutually exclusive. Preserve start, verify, recover, and native verify complete:true. Add complete(runId, rationale, evidence) for common completion without a checkpoint argument; amend(runId, amendmentId, rationale, explicit additions/replacements); bind(runId, checkpointId, reviewWorkItemId, reviewRound) for existing verifiable review results; authorize(operation, runId or execution descriptor, authorityId, userMessageId and scoped authority fields); and record_approval(runId, authorityId, approvalId, stage, artifactPath, artifactSha256, evidence). Recover on both existing tools gains optional authorityId, mutually exclusive with userMessageId. Unknown/mixed action fields fail without partial success. No new tool family or required repository artifact is introduced.

Registration and amendment rules: claim source identity by explicit executionKey and source reference; once native is selected for that identity, failed validation cannot enable generic fallback. Native preparation stores authority/source selection only and cannot launch implementation before approved native loading succeeds. Native obligations are extracted automatically and remain source-hash bound; native structural amendments require the existing source lifecycle, never the generic append path. Generic additions are append-only, within the explicit execution boundary, with canonical unique IDs, existing-or-same-batch references, acyclic task/checkpoint dependencies, and no retroactive barrier on already launched or accepted dependent work. An execution boundary may contain normalized exact files and explicitly named directory subtrees; worker writes and snapshot inputs remain exact files, with containment and symlink checks. Boundary expansion is explicit and recorded; it never expands authority automatically. Sealed executions reject all additions and implicit reopening.

Lineage: generic amend may replace one quiescent, unaccepted task with one or more explicit descendants; in-flight, accepted, or native task replacement is rejected in this increment. Preserve the parent as nonlaunchable historical work and explicitly rewrite dependent references to every required descendant. Descendants retain all parent criterion identities and their aggregate original scope; removed requirements, lost review roles, unmapped coverage, or cycles fail. Share the parent's ordinary, rework, autonomous-recovery, and advance-credit budget ledger across its descendants; a split is not a new allowance per child. A stopped/exhausted lineage still requires its existing authorized recovery path before launch. Never infer that an unrelated new key means a replacement. This explicit-identity guarantee is not semantic duplicate-task detection.

Review applicability: store exact execution/task contract revisions, accepted attempts, root, scope, reviewer call identities, and fingerprints with each review generation. A standalone review_only item can opt into a reviewContext at open time so runtime captures its snapshot before dispatch; an old unpinned report cannot be retroactively made verifiable. bind accepts only compatible recorded results for the same snapshot and roles, counts the bound generation against the ordinary checkpoint budget, and cannot overwrite a later FAIL/stop with an older PASS. Generic completion freshly validates every assigned obligation; native historical milestones retain their declared meaning and are followed by current final coverage. An assigned final checkpoint must cover all current active tasks and their write scopes. Later work cannot inherit that final approval. Complete with no reviews reports controller_accepted, never independently_reviewed; mixed or partial current review coverage is described explicitly.

Advance authority: root-controller authorize may establish a preparing execution before native files or worker tasks exist. Only an observable root-user message can grant or extend authority. Verify the exact message ID, owning root session, finite creation time, and at least one nonempty, nonignored, nonsynthetic user text part using the pinned SDK session.message response; controller judgment supplies intent, delegated stages, decision scope, execution/file boundary, and reserved stopping points. Persist metadata and bounded interpreted scope, never raw text. Refuse assistant summaries, worker messages, foreign sessions, missing identity, synthetic-only messages, and lookup failure. Reject or idempotently reuse duplicate grants without refilling; a session-wide message-claim index prevents the same originating message from funding another execution under a new key.

Authority lifecycle and recovery: initial advance reserve is exactly three units shared by the execution. An explicit extend operation with a new eligible root-user message adds exactly three further units; it is not automatic and cannot reuse a grant/extension message or predate the authority event it extends. Narrow and revoke are fail-safe reductions with provenance and cannot restore consumed units, broaden scope, delete obligations, or undo historical work. Recovery first uses remaining ordinary allowance and established bounded autonomous/rework paths; advance_grant is a distinct recorded one-unit credit after those applicable allowances are exhausted. Commit one reserve debit and one exact attempt/generation credit together, retaining diagnosis, changedCondition, and verification. Repeated/concurrent recoveryId, replacement, restart, cancellation, and rework cannot refund or duplicate a debit. Revocation blocks later grants and unlaunched advance credits; it does not abort live work or erase results. The existing post-stop userMessageId timing validator remains intact and is not reused with weakened timing for advance authority.

Native stage provenance: allow specification, planning, implementation, and verification stages only when delegated; publication, destructive/external operations, credential access, and human-reserved gates are not implied. Keep native draft/approved/applied statuses and existing element syntax. Managed skills validate the document and source rules, then use a bounded XML comment identifying controller_delegated, execution, authority, and approval IDs when marking a stage approved under authority; comments do not grant permission. record_approval checks the actual approved artifact hash and current authority/stage boundary and persists the approval record before later execution may rely on it. The native adapter rejects a delegated-provenance marker with absent, stale, mismatched, or uncommitted records. Failed recording leaves progression blocked and is not reported as approval success. Old unmarked native artifacts remain compatible with unspecified historical provenance, not invented personal human review. Inline/classic skills retain their own implementation/verification lifecycle; a stage-authorization record alone never manufactures delegated task acceptance.

Availability and permission boundary: make the existing control tools available to eligible primary root vv-controller sessions while workflow is enabled, independent of whether requirements came from a native package or whether the current profile permits implementation delegation. Apply the existing root-session, agent, trusted-workspace, and invalid-persistence checks to every new mutation, including execution-bound open and pinned review open. Tool availability is not permission to violate the active ownership policy; single-session remains direct work with permitted independent reviews, and delegated remains worker-owned implementation. Never change host permission rules, tracked identities, configured models, or startup configuration to implement this distinction.

Durability: write snapshot version 4 and explicitly migrate valid versions 1, 2, and 3. Do not use version < current as a blanket instruction to erase recovery histories: v3 already owns meaningful grants, rejected reports, and stopped generations. Maintain one authoritative execution registry with compatibility views for existing native plan-run consumers. Legacy work without executions remains legacy; old native runs remain native with the same IDs, hashes, obligations, histories, and counters. New authority is empty unless genuinely recorded. Preserve v1 snapshot-fingerprint semantics for existing native generations; introduce a versioned contract-aware fingerprint for generic/amended coverage, never relabel old hashes as new evidence. Invalid, contradictory, cross-session, or unsupported state fails closed. Missing provenance for a proposed grant rejects that operation without resetting otherwise valid work.

Atomic integration: serialize mutating operations per session, clone the latest committed state inside that serialization boundary, run asynchronous lookups/snapshot reads without publishing staged mutations, revalidate target/authority/coverage before commit, atomically persist, then synchronously publish the new live state. All touched work-item, execution, review, authority, counter, and key-index changes commit together. Include task hooks, checkpoint reviewer results, terminal failures/report rejection, recovery, acceptance, close, register, amend, and seal in the same commit discipline. Read-only inspection may show the previous committed state, never a partially accepted or newly authorized one. Do not restore a pre-await entry over a newer concurrent result or swap in an obsolete whole-store clone. This local mutation queue is not a new work scheduler.

Task graph and verification: T-002 and T-004 both depend on the common contract in T-001 but do not depend on each other. T-003 consumes T-002's registry, T-005 integrates T-003 and T-004, and subsequent delivery/audit/projection tasks consume the implemented behavior. Shared-file writes still require serialization, even where behavioral dependencies permit parallel preparation. Keep native compatibility wrappers usable while internal seams land, and do not expose an incomplete generic or authority operation before T-005. Update local contracts/maps/change summaries before each source/test edit. Durable graph and verification are reconciled centrally in T-008 rather than by parallel workers.

Scenario audit: no-document implementation must select conversation-scoped work and permit explicit no-review acceptance; delegated preparation with reserved specification approval must produce a draft and stop there; fully delegated native progression may move through authorized stages with controller_delegated provenance; a bounded prototype may use disclosed reversible choices without asking at every fork; implementation with publication excluded must never publish; discussion-only must remain discussion without task dispatch or files. Inspect the combined controller, active orchestration policy, workflow guidance, skill discovery metadata, and loaded skill bodies for every scenario. Include independent no-files/no-subagents/no-intermediate-questions combinations. These are deterministic delivery checks and an instruction audit, not measured model effectiveness.

Acceptance coverage: AC-01/02/04/05 map to T-001/002/005/007; AC-03 to T-001/003/005/007; AC-06/07/08/09/10 to T-002/003/005/007; AC-11/14/15/16/17 to T-002/004/005/007; AC-12/13 to T-004/005/006/007; AC-18/19/20/21 to T-006/007/008; AC-22 to T-001 through T-005 and T-007; AC-23 to T-006/007; AC-24 to the exercised baseline, T-008, and T-009. The exact three-unit initial reserve is approved specification policy, not a benchmark-derived optimum. Optional sandbox model smoke runs require isolation and explicit reporting of whether they were performed; no evaluation platform is added.

Final review obligation R-001: after T-001 through T-008 are accepted, obtain one independent spec review and one independent code review over the pinned combined result, approved spec/plan, test evidence, and instruction audit. This obligation belongs to this risky implementation and is not a universal final-review default for the product. A findings-only FAIL is not passing acceptance. Validate findings personally; corrections remain within the original task scopes and require fresh checks and applicable re-review. BLOCKED and NEEDS_CONTEXT suspend the affected work. GRACE target/final lint and status are external lifecycle gates, never nested MustPassCommand values; current assertions run only before observed writes.

Read current local contracts before editing and update their dependency links. Do not change public exports, XML syntax, configured roles, or source registration behavior yet.

Define the common source, task, checkpoint, execution boundary, revision, lineage, and authority/stage record shapes described in PlanningNotes, with discriminated source variants and canonical spec/code requiredReviewers. Generic validation accepts arbitrary bounded explicit IDs, not only TASK-T-NNN or WAVE-N native names, and requires no source paths or wave list.

Move the pure normalizeDeclaredScopePath contract unchanged into the common module and retain its existing spec-lint export as a compatibility re-export. Reuse it in every runtime consumer; snapshot filesystem checks, absent-file handling, mode/content/attempt hashing, and symlink rejection remain in snapshots.ts.

Provide common validation for unique IDs, bounded nonempty task contracts, explicit reviewer arrays, normalized file/directory boundaries, exact references, containment, and cycles across tasks and checkpoint prerequisites. Explicit [] means no independent review for a delegated task; absent/malformed requiredReviewers is not normalized silently to [].

Native extraction still runs strict approved plan/spec validation, cross-file component checks, archive/root checks, source hashes, declared wave barriers, and final task/scope coverage before producing a common contract. Lift existing task acceptance, verification, and dependency text from the validated native source instead of inventing generic requirements. Preserve legacy extraction callers with compatible exports and native metadata.

Diagnostic scenarios distinguish one generic task with no files describing requirements from an invalid selected native package: the former validates its explicit task contract without XML, while missing approval, invalid native references, or altered source hashes remain native errors. Scope traversal/wildcard/duplicate and cyclic dependency fixtures fail for both input paths; valid native fixtures keep their syntax and extracted obligations.

T-002.Title: Introduce one durable execution registry with incremental contracts and explicit replacement lineage.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create workflow/execution.ts and execution.test.ts under M-WORKFLOW-EXECUTION. Modify workflow/state.ts, delegated.ts and its test, checkpoints.ts, checkpoint-io.ts, persistence.ts and its test, plus native-facing references in workflow/index.ts and workflow.test.ts only as needed to keep existing consumers working. The common registry replaces native-only assumptions; do not add a second untracked execution engine or expose unfinished generic tools.

Register preparing/active executions with immutable source identity and an explicit key, session, and trusted root. Native existing registration adapts into this registry and retains run IDs and source hashes. Generic registration can atomically bind one task, a batch, or an exact compatible unbound work item, preserving counters and acceptance histories. Reject source switching, duplicate conflicting identities, foreign-session/run adoption, mismatched scopes/contracts, and native fallback after failure for the same identity.

Append tasks and requirements without replaying accepted work. Validate all same-batch dependencies before any item/key index is published; rollback the entire batch on one invalid item. Reject unknown references, cycles, writes outside the boundary, additions to a sealed run, and retroactive barriers for already launched dependents. Store origin, amendmentId, previous/new revision, rationale, and affected requirement/review identities.

Support explicit replacement/splitting only for quiescent unaccepted generic tasks, retaining parent history and aggregate original criteria/scope. Rewire explicit dependents and coverage without dropping obligations. Share the parent's consumed and remaining attempt/rework/recovery budget across all descendants, including the single autonomous allowance. No child receives fresh base attempts merely because it has a new taskId. Accepted, live, or native replacements, unmapped criteria, or weakened reviews fail without mutation.

Introduce snapshot v4 for the execution registry and its declared authority fields, initially empty until genuine authorization. Explicitly preserve all v3 recovery/rejected-report/stopped-generation data; v2 adds only the previously absent empty recovery histories, and v1 remains legacy. Keep old standalone records unbound and native runs native; compatibility views must refer to the same authoritative objects. Strictly validate source discriminants, keys, references, revision/lineage acyclicity, counters, and cross-session identity.

Regression scenarios cover accepting a first task, adding a second without losing acceptance, cyclic-batch rollback, same-key source switching, native run migration, exact unbound-item adoption, and splitting an exhausted task without gaining any attempts. Round-trip each scenario through v4 and separately hydrate fixed v1/v2/v3 fixtures, including a v3 consumed grant that must not disappear after the version bump.

T-003.Title: Enforce dynamic review obligations, exact result reuse, and fresh common completion.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Modify workflow/execution.ts and its test, checkpoints.ts and its test, state.ts, transitions.ts, delegated.ts and its test, snapshots.ts and its test, persistence.ts and its test, and native compatibility linkage in workflow/index.ts and workflow.test.ts. Reuse the T-002 registry and T-001 contracts; do not implement another review state machine or change tracked result protocol grammar.

Register per-task and group review obligations without a source file, storing their origins and exact requiredReviewers. Per-task acceptance remains distinct: DONE waits for the controller, and an assigned review still blocks dependent work and completion after accept. Both reviewers must actually report when both were assigned. Legacy review_only FAIL remains closeable findings, never a passing implementation obligation.

Use task dependencies and explicit blockedBy edges for generic launches, and retain native adapter-produced wave barriers. Checkpoint start requires current acceptance of covered tasks, a nonempty registered reviewer set, no overlapping in-flight review/write scope, and remaining generation budget. Capture task/criterion revisions and accepted attempts with the file snapshot; preserve generation-bound reviewer call IDs and hard stops.

Capture optional reviewContext at standalone review_only open before dispatch. Bind only exact stored round/call/snapshot evidence to a compatible checkpoint; do not trust a caller-supplied hash or prose claim. Reject missing pre-review snapshots, wrong root/attempt/contract/scope, unassigned roles, stale content, and an older PASS offered to erase a later failed/stopped generation. Binding consumes one generation and preserves existing reviewer-result identity rather than dispatching a duplicate review.

Complete generic executions only when every active task is currently accepted, replacement lineage and requirements remain accounted for, and every assigned review barrier has applicable results. No final checkpoint is required when none was assigned. An assigned final checkpoint requires current complete task/scope coverage and fresh fingerprints even if its previous status is already passed. Native historical milestones and mandatory final coverage retain their source-defined meaning.

Later task additions, amended criteria, new accepted attempts, or changed reviewed files cannot inherit stale final approval. An explicit in-scope coverage amendment may expand the same generic final obligation while retaining history and consumed generation budget; it cannot install a fresh counter. Report controller_accepted for a no-review result and distinguish historical/mixed coverage from independent review of the complete current result.

Counterexamples: closed review-only FAIL; accept followed by skipped required reviewer; PASS followed by a file edit and later complete:true; PASS followed by a new task; reviewContext mismatch; exhausted checkpoint re-registered under the same identity; and a no-review execution that should complete. Verify native and generic success through the same reducers, plus retained two-generation limits and historical v1 fingerprint interpretation.

T-004.Title: Implement the bounded advance-authority and approval-provenance domain.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create only workflow/authority.ts and authority.test.ts under M-WORKFLOW-AUTHORITY, consuming the common contract. Keep the module independent of native XML parsing, SDK transport, task dispatch, and filesystem writes. It returns explicit validation outcomes and proposed ledger transitions; runtime integration belongs to T-005.

Implement grant, extend, narrow, revoke, stage-approval validation, and one-unit reserve consumption with execution/session/source/scope binding. Initial grant records ADVANCE_RECOVERY_RESERVE = 3, root-user message identity/timing, delegated stages, decision scope, and reserved stops. Another initial grant for the same execution or a replay under another execution key cannot create another reserve.

Advance provenance requires exact observable root-user identity and nonsynthetic, nonignored user input; message text interpretation stays with the controller. Missing/foreign/assistant/synthetic-only/unverifiable provenance returns a bounded error and cannot grant authority. An explicit new extension adds three units once, is bound to the same execution, and uses a new eligible instruction after the authority event being extended, not the old post-stop validator.

Reserve consumption creates one immutable consumption identity and exact target credit; duplicate consumption/recovery IDs and concurrent last-unit proposals cannot debit twice or allocate two credits. A task replacement retains the same execution/lineage budget. Narrowing/revocation does not remove past approvals or consumed units; it disables future and unlaunched out-of-scope credits without aborting an already running attempt.

Stage checks distinguish controller_delegated action from unspecified legacy or personally observed user approval. Reserved specification/plan approval and publication stops block their corresponding transition. Implementation authority alone does not grant destructive, external, publication, credential, or permission-override authority. Preparing an artifact is not permission to execute it.

Test one pre-stop grant, three credits shared across two task targets and a checkpoint, denied fourth credit, duplicate initial registration, exact replay across execution keys, extension with a fresh message, narrowing, revocation, foreign authority, and reserved-stage approval. These are pure contract tests, not claims that runtime can classify natural-language autonomy reliably.

T-005.Title: Expose the generic tools and integrate authority through atomic SDK-backed workflow transactions.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Create workflow/transactions.ts and transactions.test.ts under M-PLUGIN-WORKFLOW. Modify workflow/tooling.ts, index.ts, state.ts, delegated.ts and its test, checkpoints.ts and its test, execution.ts and its test, authority.ts and its test, persistence.ts and its test, checkpoint-io.ts and its test, workflow.test.ts, and workflow.delegated.test.ts. Keep new action fields/types shared between the domain wrappers and the plugin's actual tool schema.

Implement the additive work_item_open, work_item_decide, and work_checkpoint contracts in PlanningNotes, including one-call generic startup, atomic batch append, dynamic registration, exact review binding, common complete, explicit amend, and advance/stage controls. Return canonical run/task/checkpoint identities, source mode, required obligations, available budgets, committed provenance, honest acceptance/review status, and supported next actions. Keep old native calls and existing standalone/legacy work items usable.

Register the existing control tools for eligible root vv-controller sessions independent of orchestration profile, but do not change ownership policies or host permissions. Apply root, agent, trusted-workspace, and invalid-hydration checks to every new mutation, execution-bound open, and pinned review open. Native selected-source errors remain explicit; generic paths never invoke loadApprovedDelegatedPlan or execute source/verification text.

Use the pinned SDK client.session.message({path:{id,messageID},query:{directory}}) response info and parts, and session.get root identity, for provenance. Derive fixtures from SessionMessageResponses, UserMessage, TextPart, and ToolContext, retaining only verified identity/timing/eligibility metadata. A missing/failed authorization lookup rejects only that grant or extension without resetting valid workflow work. Existing post-stop userMessageId timing and per-target recovery history remain meaningful.

Integrate advance_grant into task and checkpoint recovery only after applicable existing allowances are exhausted, retaining diagnosis, changedCondition, verification, and exact recoveryId. Debit the execution ledger and grant one target attempt/generation in the same commit. Keep autonomous grants, checkpoint-authorized rework, advance reserve, and fresh post-stop user grants distinguishable; none accepts work, satisfies a reviewer, or clears a hard stop without a recorded bounded recovery.

Serialize mutations per session and stage from the latest committed store, including hook-driven launch/result/failure/rejected-report transitions and control calls. Persist atomically before publishing acceptance, obligations, lineage, source claims, counters, stage records, or launch credits. On write/rename failure the prior committed state remains observable; no success or dispatch permission leaks. Avoid stale clone replacement or pre-await rollback over a concurrent mutation; preserve live call bindings and fail-closed ambiguous host outcomes.

Persist and strictly validate v4 authority events, session-wide message claims, reserve debits, target credits, revocations, stage approvals, source selection, and dynamic review links together. Validate cross-record totals, chronology, exact target bindings, replay uniqueness, and granted-versus-usable credit distinction. Restart never refunds consumed reserve or invents authority from historical native approved statuses.

Enable authority before native artifacts exist without making a preparing execution runnable. record_approval verifies the actual marked approved artifact, its hash, stage, scope, and recorded authority; native loading checks marked provenance against the committed record.
